name: Maisie's Galaxy
note: One of the first z>11 galaxies spectroscopically confirmed by JWST; named after Finkelstein's daughter. Coords from name CEERS J141946.36+525632.8 (14:19:46.36, +52:56:32.8) - VERIFY against CEERS catalog.

name: GN-z11
note: Luminous z=10.6 galaxy, longtime distance record-holder pre-JWST; N-rich UV spectrum. Coords from 12:36:25.46 +62:14:31.4.

name: CEERS-93316
note: Famous z_phot~16.4 candidate later revised to a z=4.91 dusty galaxy - cautionary tale. Coords 14:19:39.48 +52:56:34.92.

name: JADES-GS-z14-0
ref: Carniani+2024; z spec refined by ALMA [OIII]88um (Carniani+2025, Schouws+2025)
note: Current most-distant spectroscopically confirmed galaxy (z=14.18). Coords 03:32:19.905 -27:51:20.27.

name: JADES-GS-z14-1
note: Faintest spectroscopically confirmed galaxy at z~14. Coords 03:32:17.825 -27:53:09.34 (from designation). z 13.86-13.90 across papers.

name: JADES-GS-z13-0
note: One of first four z>10 galaxies spectroscopically confirmed by JWST; was distance record-holder 2022-2024. Coords 03:32:35.97 -27:46:35.4.

name: JADES-GS-z12-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations. NEEDS COORDS - in JADES Origins Field near z11-0/z13-0 (RA~53.15, Dec~-27.77); could not extract exact position from a primary source.

name: JADES-GS-z11-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations. Coords from designation.

name: JADES-GS-z10-0
note: One of the original four Curtis-Lake z>10 confirmations; historically the UDFj z-drop. NEEDS COORDS - in JADES Origins Field; exact position not extracted from primary source.

name: JADES-GS-z13-1
note: z~13 galaxy with strong Lyman-alpha damping-wing / possible Lyman-alpha; probes reionization. Coords 03:32:15.57 -27:53:23.29.

name: MoM-z14
ref: Naidu+2025 ('A Cosmic Miracle', Open J. Astrophys.)
note: Most distant spectroscopically confirmed galaxy as of 2025 (z=14.44); first result from the 'Mirage or Miracle' survey in COSMOS. Coords 10:00:22.40 +02:16:23.19.

name: GHZ2
note: Luminous z=12.3 galaxy behind Abell 2744; one of the brightest known ultra-high-z sources. Coords 00:13:59.76 -30:19:29.1.

name: GHZ1
note: Bright z~9.9 galaxy behind Abell 2744, early GLASS-JWST z>10 candidate.

name: GHZ9
note: z=10.1 source in Abell 2744 with an X-ray-detected accreting SMBH (dual AGN + star formation).

name: UNCOVER-z13
note: Lensed z~13 galaxy behind Abell 2744 (tentative spec confirmation via break).

name: UNCOVER-z12
note: Lensed z=12.4 galaxy behind Abell 2744.

name: Abell2744-QSO1
note: Prototypical 'little red dot' - a triply-lensed, reddened z=7.04 AGN with ~50M-solar SMBH; high BH-to-host mass ratio. Coords are brightest image A (Furtak+2025 Table 1); NASA press RA/Dec 00:14:18.25 -30:22:46.04 differs slightly (different image / centroid).

name: CEERS 1019
note: Hosted the most distant confirmed accreting SMBH at the time (z=8.68, 570 Myr after Big Bang); originally EGSY8p7. Coords 14:20:08.494 +52:53:26.

name: CEERS-2112
note: Most distant barred spiral galaxy found; a young Milky-Way analog / progenitor at z=3.

name: GNz7q
note: Dust-reddened compact quasar precursor bridging starbursts and quasars at cosmic dawn in GOODS-N. Coords 12:36:16.85 +62:12:31.98 (ESA/Hubble).

name: Gz9p3
note: Bright interacting/merging system at z=9.3 lensed by Abell 2744 periphery (mu~1.7). FIELD CORRECTION: it is A2744-lensed, NOT GOODS-N. One follow-up paper lists ~3.607, -30.381 (differs ~arcmin) - VERIFY exact centroid via MAST/NED.

name: The Cliff
note: Famous 'little red dot' in PRIMER-UDS with the strongest Balmer break yet seen plus broad H-alpha; the most notable nicknamed UDS object. Coords 02:17:38.58 -05:07:46.79.

name: COSMOS-Web ring
note: Serendipitous Einstein ring in COSMOS-Web; massive quiescent elliptical lens (z_lens~2.0) around a z=5.10 spec source. Coords name-derived (arcsec-level, 10:00:24 +01:53:34) - refine for sub-arcsec use. z listed is the lensed background source; lens itself z~2.0 phot.

name: Cosmic Grapes
note: Quintuply-imaged rotating disk resolved into ~15 star-forming clumps ('grapes') at z=6.07. FIELD: lensed by cluster RXCJ0600-2007, NOT COSMOS. Multiply-imaged near 06:00:09 -20:08; no single canonical source J2000 position - null flagged.

name: Firefly Sparkle
note: Lensed Milky-Way-progenitor arc resolved into individual star clusters at z=8.3. FIELD: lensed by MACS J1423.8+2404, NOT A2744. Arc position not tabulated in primary paper - null flagged (cluster ~14:23:47 +24:04).

name: GLIMPSE-16a
note: Robust z~16.4 photometric candidate behind lensing cluster Abell S1063. FIELD: Abell S1063, NOT A2744. Unconfirmed - would break the z=14 spec record if confirmed.

name: GLIMPSE-16b
note: Robust z~15.8 photometric candidate behind Abell S1063. FIELD: Abell S1063, NOT A2744. Unconfirmed.
